predecessors.name: Sulayhid dynasty
predecessors.text: Aden and the Lahij oasis, ruled by the Banu Ma'n until the brothers were placed in power in 1083

successors.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
successors.text: Aden and the Zurayid lands, conquered 22 June 1174 by Turan Shah

rulers.name: Abi Saud bin Zuray and Saba bin Abi Saud
Muhammad bin Imran and Abi Saud bin Imran

ledger.x: 1083: the brothers al-Abbas and al-Mas'ud are set over Aden.

c. 1148: the inland line of Muhammad bin Saba buys the highland fortresses and towns round Ibb. Page: 'The two lines met in open warfare in 1138' and 'A decade later the ruler Muhammad bin Saba bought a number of important Sulayhid fortresses and towns' (Dhu Jibla, al-Takar, Ibb, Habb), after marrying the last…
ledger.cp: Sulayhid remnant (holders of the highland fortresses)

ledger.x: 1174: the Ayyubids take Aden and end the Zurayids.

wars.name: Siege of Zabid (1110)
wars.outcome: The Zurayid brothers joined the Sulayhid al-Mufaddal's campaign against Zabid and were both killed in the siege; the Zurayids ruled Aden independently for more than sixty years afterwards.

wars.name: Zurayid civil war
wars.outcome: 'The two lines met in open warfare in 1138' and the coastal line of al-Msaod was pushed out of Aden; Ali bin Abi al-Gharat of that line 'was killed in the battle of Za'za' in Lahij in 1150' and the inland line of al-Abbas ruled alone.

wars.name: Mahdid siege of Aden
wars.outcome: The Mahdids of Zabid besieged Aden in 1164; with the Hamdanid sultan of Sana'a's help the Zurayids 'utterly defeat the Mahdid ruler Abd an-Nabi in 1173'.

wars.name: Ayyubid conquest of Aden
wars.outcome: The Ayyubids conquered Aden on 22 June 1174, ending the Zurayids.

certainty.note: Aden is a city-port and Lahij a named plain; the highland holdings after c.
